input.quote: 7. LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.
input.rationale: Section 7 is headed "INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR" but contains no operative indemnity language at all; a full-text search for "indemnif" and "hold harmless" returns only the heading. There is therefore no Contractor/Vendor indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of law, data breach, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct. Section 5(c) gives only a non-infringement warranty, which is subject to the Section 7(a) fees cap and the Section 7(c) attorneys' fee waiver and does not provide defence of third-party claims. This falls at the playbook walk-away position (no Vendor IP indemnity). We insert the preferred Vendor indemnity as new Section 7(d), with standard notice/control/cooperation procedure and a carve-out from the Section 7(a) cap and 7(c) fee waiver. No Customer indemnity exists, so nothing needs narrowing.

proposal.summary: Insert a Contractor (Vendor) indemnity as new Section 7(d) covering IP infringement, breach of law, data/confidentiality breach and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with standard defence procedure and carve-out from the Section 7(a) cap and 7(c) fee waiver.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement contains no indemnity at all (Section 7's heading even promises indemnification of Contractor), so we have added a Contractor indemnity for third-party IP infringement claims, breach of law, Contractor-caused data or confidentiality breaches, and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with standard notice/control/cooperation procedure. Our playbook requires this protection to sit with the party that controls the Services and IP; if needed we can accept the usual IP exclusions (our modifications, combinations, specifications) and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, with the indemnity capped at 3x annual fees.

ops.text: (d) INDEMNIFICATION BY CONTRACTOR. Contractor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Company and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (i) an allegation that the Services or Works infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (ii) Contractor's breach of applicable law; (iii) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Company's Confidential Information or data caused by Contractor; or (iv) Contractor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Company shall give Contractor prompt written notice of the claim, Contractor shall have control of the defense and settlement (provided that no settlement that imposes any obligation, payment or admission on Company shall be made without Company's prior written consent), and Company shall provide reasonable cooperation at Contractor's expense. Notwithstanding Sections 7(a) and 7(c), Contractor's obligations under this Section 7(d) are not subject to the limitation of liability in Section 7(a) or the waiver of attorneys' fees in Section 7(c).
